text: For the California Controller race, Malia Cohen has not called the war in Gaza a genocide, has not backed blocking weapons transfers, and has not taken divestment action on the record. What she has done is earn the endorsement of CAIR Action and the support of Vote for Peace, organizations that evaluate candidates on civil-rights and war-lobby criteria. Her Republican opponent, Herb Morgan, attended the Friends of the IDF Golf Tournament on April 29, 2026, publicly framing his presence as standing with allies who defend freedom and reinforcing security and global leadership. Cohen's platform for the office centers on managing the eight-hundred-billion-dollar CalPERS and CalSTRS portfolios, expanding affordable housing, and protecting reproductive healthcare access. Neither candidate has delivered the specific legislative acts the two litmus tests demand, but Morgan's shown record on Gaza is a single public appearance at an IDF event, while Cohen's alignment with Palestinian-rights organizations at least signals she is not publicly celebrating that military. That contrast makes Cohen the stronger of the two on the record presented.
